For \(n=14\),

Let \(C\) be the circle in the complex plane with centre \(z_0=\frac{1}{2}(1+3 i)\) and radius \(r=1\). Let \(z_1=1+i\) and the complex number \(z_2\) be outside the circle \(C\) such that \(\left|z_1-z_0\right|\left|z_2-z_0\right|=1\). [JEE Main 2023, 12 Apr (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
The centre of the circle is \(z_0=\dfrac{1+3i}{2}\), and \(z_1=1+i\).

First calculate the distance of \(z_1\) from the centre.

We have \(z_1-z_0=1+i-\dfrac{1+3i}{2}=\dfrac{1-i}{2}\).

Therefore, \(|z_1-z_0|=\dfrac{|1-i|}{2}=\dfrac{\sqrt{1^2+(-1)^2}}{2}=\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\).

Given \(|z_1-z_0|\,|z_2-z_0|=1\), we get \(\dfrac1{\sqrt2}|z_2-z_0|=1\).

Thus \(|z_2-z_0|=\sqrt2\).

The complex number \(z_1-z_0=\dfrac{1-i}{2}\) gives the direction of the line through \(z_0\) and \(z_1\).

A unit complex number in this direction is \(\dfrac{z_1-z_0}{|z_1-z_0|}=\dfrac{1-i}{\sqrt2}\).

Since \(z_0,z_1,z_2\) are collinear and \(|z_2-z_0|=\sqrt2\), the two possible points are \(z_2=z_0\pm\sqrt2\left(\dfrac{1-i}{\sqrt2}\right)\).

Hence \(z_2=z_0\pm(1-i)\).

For the positive sign, \(z_2=\dfrac{1+3i}{2}+1-i=\dfrac{3+i}{2}\).

For the negative sign, \(z_2=\dfrac{1+3i}{2}-1+i=\dfrac{-1+5i}{2}\).

Now \(\left|\dfrac{3+i}{2}\right|^2=\dfrac{3^2+1^2}{4}=\dfrac52\).

Also, \(\left|\dfrac{-1+5i}{2}\right|^2=\dfrac{(-1)^2+5^2}{4}=\dfrac{13}{2}\).

Therefore, the smaller value of \(|z_2|^2\) is \(\dfrac52\), and the correct option is \(\mathrm{B}\).

[JEE Main 2023, 12 Apr (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
In this case, the success is defined as getting a number less than \(n\) when rolling an \(n\)-sided die. The probability of success, \(p\), in each roll is then \(\frac{(n-1)} { n}\), and the probability of failure, \(q=1-p\), is \(\frac{1} { n}\).

Mean \(=\sum_{i=1}^{\infty} p_i x_i\)

Mean =1⋅n−1n+21nn−1n+31n2n−1n

n9=n−1n1+21n+31n2……

∵1−x−n=1+nx+n(n+1)2x2+…

n9=n−1n1−1n−2=n−1n⋅n2(n−1)2

n9=nn−1⇒n=10
